rationale: Iteration 0 has no race telemetry, so this is a conservative baseline meant to produce the first measurements, not a tuned design. Geometry: five line sensors spaced 0.02 m apart across x = -0.04 to +0.04 and placed 0.03 m ahead of the axle, so the steering signal is measured slightly ahead of the wheels. Sensor size 0.012 m is about half the 25 mm tape width, which gives a clean, graded response as the line moves under the array. Wheel track 0.12 m and radius 0.03 m are mid-range, and mass 0.8 kg keeps yaw inertia moderate. Controller: sensor weights are linear in x (-1, -0.5, 0, 0.5, 1), so signal is about the line's lateral offset, positive meaning left. kp = 2.5 gives a moderate steering response (signal 1 produces a 875 PWM differential), ki = 0 avoids integral windup on curves, and kd = 0.1 adds light damping against oscillation. base_speed = 1.8 is high enough to approach the 1.5 m/s average needed to finish in 3 s, but leaves margin below full drive. line_loss = last_direction so the robot searches toward the side it last saw the line. Expected result: completion on the oval and s-bend with a small rms_error. The main risks are overshoot on the slalom and off-track exits on tight bends at this speed. Hypotheses to check next: (1) if the robot oscillates, kp is too high or kd too low; (2) if it leaves the line on bends, speed is too high or kp too low; (3) if it is too slow to finish, base_speed should rise. The next measurements to see are completion_time, max_error, steering_oscillation and line_loss_events per track.
